articles.title: ‘The Good Place’ actor Ted Danson helped build Oceana; how a Hollywood star turned an oil-drilling fight into a global ocean conservation organisation
articles.summary: Ted Danson is widely recognised for his television roles in Cheers and The Good Place, but his work beyond Hollywood has helped shape an international
articles.body: Ted Danson is widely recognised for his television roles in Cheers and The Good Place, but his work beyond Hollywood has helped shape an international movement for ocean protection. The actor's environmental activism began in California during the 1980s, when a proposed offshore oil drilling project threatened the coastline near his home. What started as a neighbourhood campaign eventually led to the creation of the American Oceans Campaign and, later, his involvement with Oceana, an organisation working to protect marine life and restore the world's oceans. His journey illustrates how celebrity influence can support long-term environmental action.Ted Danson turned an oil-drilling fight into an ocean conservation movementDanson's involvement in ocean conservation began with a problem close to home. According to the Cornell Chronicle, he became interested in protecting the ocean in 1982 after moving to a California neighbourhood where residents were fighting to prevent oil drilling near their beach.The proposal involved offshore drilling near Santa Monica Bay, and Danson joined local residents in opposing it. Rather than limiting his involvement to expressing concern, he helped organise the community and worked to bring the issue to a citywide ballot.The campaign proved successful. Danson's 2009 written testimony before the US House Committee on Natural Resources explained that he had teamed up with an environmental expert to fight Occidental Petroleum's proposed slant drilling off Santa Monica in the late 1980s. The effort succeeded, preventing the project from proceeding.The experience demonstrated to Danson that organised public action could influence environmental decisions. It also gave him a reason to continue working beyond a single local campaign.From the American Oceans Campaign to OceanaThe next step was to turn local activism into a more organised effort. Oceana's official Ted Danson profile says he helped establish the American Oceans Campaign in 1987, following the Santa Monica victory. The organisation was created to continue protecting the oceans from oil drilling and other environmental threats.Danson and environmental lawyer Robert Sulnick were central to this effort. As he later explained in an interview with Impacting Our Future, the campaign began on a small scale, operating from their basement before developing a stronger presence in Washington.The Cornell Chronicle reported that Danson hired a lobbyist and began advocating for ocean conservation in the US capital. His involvement also evolved beyond campaigning against oil companies. He came to believe that environmental protection required engagement with businesses rather than treating them exclusively as opponents.That approach shaped the campaign's work. Danson recalled working with oil company executives on a used motor oil recycling programme, even while continuing to challenge them on other environmental issues. The experience reinforced his view that cooperation could produce practical results without abandoning conservation goals.Oceana was founded in 2001 as an international organisation focused exclusively on ocean conservation. The American Oceans Campaign subsequently merged with Oceana in 2002, expanding its capacity to work internationally. Danson initially considered leaving the movement after the merger, but meeting its scientists, lawyers and advocates persuaded him to remain involved.Why ocean protection became a broader environmental missionDanson's activism gradually moved beyond the immediate question of offshore drilling. In his 2009 congressional testimony, he argued that oil and gas development threatened marine wildlife, coastal communities and the livelihoods connected to the sea.He highlighted the risks of oil spills, routine pollution and damage to marine habitats. His testimony also connected offshore drilling with climate change, pointing to the oceans' role in absorbing carbon dioxide and the dangers of increasing ocean acidity.The economic argument was equally important. Danson noted that commercial and recreational fisheries supported millions of jobs in the United States, while coastal tourism generated substantial employment and economic activity. Protecting the oceans, he argued, was not simply about wildlife but also about safeguarding communities and livelihoods.His testimony urged Congress to restore restrictions on offshore drilling and invest in cleaner ocean-based energy, including wind, tidal and wave power.How Danson uses his Hollywood platform for ocean advocacyHis acting career has given Danson a public platform that few environmental campaigners possess. Rather than attempting to become the scientific voice of conservation, he has used his visibility to introduce experts and environmental issues to wider audiences.His role has involved drawing attention to conservation work while allowing scientists and campaigners to explain the problems in greater depth.In an interview with Impacting Our Future, Danson described his responsibility as learning about environmental issues and making use of the cameras and microphones available to him. He also acknowledged that celebrity activism should not overshadow the contributions of scientists and ordinary people working in their communities.What Oceana has achieved since its international expansionOceana's work has grown considerably since the American Oceans Campaign joined the organisation. Global Heroes reported in its 25th anniversary coverage that Oceana had expanded its campaigns across 10 coastal countries and the European Union, protecting more than 4 million square miles of ocean and achieving over 350 policy victories.Its campaigns address several threats, including overfishing, destructive fishing practices, offshore drilling, plastic pollution and the loss of marine habitats. The organisation has also worked to improve transparency in commercial fishing and protect threatened species.One of the initiatives Danson highlighted in the Global Heroes interview was Global Fishing Watch, developed by Oceana, SkyTruth and Google. The platform allows people to monitor commercial fishing vessels in near real time. Danson said it had made around one-third of the world's industrial fishing fleet trackable, helping governments identify illegal fishing and harmful practices.He also pointed to newer fishing equipment designed to reduce whale entanglement. On-demand fishing gear allows ropes to surface only when fishers are ready to retrieve their equipment, reducing the danger posed by traditional vertical lines.Restoring the oceans remains Danson's long-term goalIn his Global Heroes interview, Danson emphasised that marine ecosystems can recover when they receive sufficient protection and time. He cited improvements in the proportion of waters protected in countries where Oceana works, alongside efforts to establish science-based fishing limits in Chile, the European Union and Brazil.Danson continues to serve on Oceana's Board of Directors alongside his wife, actress Mary Steenburgen, according to the organisation's official profile.You use AI every day. articles.title: 400+ MBBS seats find no takers even after special vacancy round
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: As many as 411 MBBS seats remained unallotted even after the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) conducted a special stray vacancy round, with
articles.body: NEW DELHI: As many as 411 MBBS seats remained unallotted even after the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) conducted a special stray vacancy round, with the high fee structure in private medical colleges potentially being one of the factors behind the seats remaining unfilled. Of the 948 vacant MBBS seats included in the special round's seat matrix, only 537 were allotted, leaving 411 unfilled. These vacancies raise questions about the affordability of medical education, particularly in private colleges where fees can run into lakhs of rupees.High costs may have deterred some NEET-qualified candidates from opting for these seats, although the allotment data does not establish the reasons for individual choices.A health ministry official said last year, only around 60-70 MBBS seats had remained vacant. "SC had directed us to conduct four rounds of counselling, but we conducted a fifth round as well. Despite that, more than 400 seats remain without allotments.""In many institutions, fees that were around at Rs 15 lakh have increased to Rs 25 lakh to Rs 30 lakh. Govt medical college seats and those in reputed private institutions are getting filled. Vacancies are concentrated in some private colleges. These institutions need to review their fees structures and the quality of education and infrastructure they offer. If fees remain this high, increasing the number of seats will serve little purpose as students can't afford them," the official said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Indian Army’s four-legged robots give a new edge to border surveillance in J&K
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian Army has started a new chapter of border surveillance in Jammu & Kashmir where four-legged robots, along with their human colleagues and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian Army has started a new chapter of border surveillance in Jammu & Kashmir where four-legged robots, along with their human colleagues and military dogs, are keeping a tight vigil in difficult terrains in forward areas.Besides introducing robots, Indian Army has modernised its border surveillance through artificial intelligence, high-tech sensors, smart-fencing and satellite integration and multi-agency intelligence coordination along the Line of Control (LoC).It has also integrated laser-based counter-drone systems and laser-intrusion detection components along parts of the border in J&K.But the centre of attraction are the four-legged robotic units that have been patrolling the difficult terrains of the over 740-km-long LoC. Army received the first batch of 100 four-legged robotic units, known as MULE (multi-utility legged equipment) in June 2024 and has since extended their active deployment to sensitive border areas such as Akhnoor and Rajouri in J&K. Videos of these robotic mules patrolling in Akhnoor sector went viral recently.“Hundreds of such robotic mules have already been deployed along the LoC and border in Jammu to strengthen surveillance systems. These machines have not only provided a new edge to border security with advanced technology and real-time intelligence in high-security sectors but also helped in providing logistics in rugged and difficult terrains in forward areas,” defence sources told TOI. They also support ambush operations (during encounters with infiltrators or terrorists) and help track enemy movements.The advantage of having such four-legged robotic chassis is that they can easily navigate rugged landscapes where traditional wheeled or tracked vehicles cannot reach; they can climb mountain slopes and walk easily on 45-degree inclines, snow-clad areas, in deserts and river crossings.They have also been engineered to function reliably in harsh weather extremes, with operational temperatures typically ranging from -40°C to +55°C.The robotic units are also capable of carrying tactical payloads—of 12 kg to 15 kg -- such as ammunition, rations and fuel to reduce the physical burden on soldiers. They have been equipped with 360-degree cameras, electro-optics, thermal/infrared technology and radar systems for real-time threat detection and object recognition.

Greeting people on the occasion, he said cow protection must be ensured under all circumstances, alongside efforts to improve cattle breeds and make livestock farmers prosperous.Yogi, who arrived in Gorakhpur on Sunday for Diwali, garlanded cows, applied tilak and sought blessings for people’s well-being. articles.summary: Leopard attacked a moving motorcycle near Azamgarhpurwa in Bahraich; riders escaped unhurt as forest officials and villagers drove the animal back.
articles.body: Bahraich: Panic gripped villagers in the Nishangara Range of the Katarniaghat Wildlife Division after a leopard reportedly attacked a moving motorcycle near Azamgarhpurwa village on Sunday evening. The two riders narrowly escaped after the motorcyclist accelerated and managed to move away from the animal.According to reports, the leopard suddenly emerged from a sugarcane field near the village and pounced on the moving motorcycle. The rider, Rajkumar, a resident of Mukhiya Farm, accelerated to escape the attack and save himself and his friend.The incident has triggered fear among residents of surrounding villages, who have expressed concern over the frequent movement of leopards near human settlements.Following the incident, Gajmitras (elephant and wildlife conservation volunteers) patrolling the area immediately alerted villagers through megaphones and advised them to remain cautious.A team from the forest department also reached the spot. Forest Range Officer Ashish Gaur said a joint drive was conducted with the help of villagers and Gajmitras to drive the leopard away. The team raised a loud alarm and burst firecrackers to scare the animal. Following the operation, the leopard moved towards the forest.The forest department has appealed to residents to avoid venturing out alone during the evening hours and remain vigilant, particularly in areas adjoining sugarcane fields and forested stretches.Officials have also urged villagers to immediately inform the department about any further sightings of the leopard to ensure residents’ safety and prevent possible human-wildlife conflict.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Varanasi | Silver Rate in Varanasi | Bank Holidays in Varanasi | Public Holidays in Varanasi | Varanasi AQI | Weather in Varanasi | Petrol Price in Varanasi | Diesel Price in Varanasi | CNG Price in Varanasi | LPG Price in VaranasiStay updated with the latest Varanasi news. articles.title: MEA slams US court summons to Doval, RAW ex-chief Goel
articles.summary: New Delhi: Govt on Tuesday dismissed a US court civil summons naming national security adviser Ajit Doval and former R&AW chief Samant Goel as a
articles.body: New Delhi: Govt on Tuesday dismissed a US court civil summons naming national security adviser Ajit Doval and former R&AW chief Samant Goel as a "frivolous lawsuit" driven by "fabricated and malicious" claims, asserting that designated Khalistani terrorist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun's legal maneuvering did not hold any merit, reports Rajshekhar Jha."...Requests for the service of judicial documents in India can only be routed through India's designated central authority, that is, the ministry of law and justice," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.MEA's reaction came on reports of the US state department notifying India via a diplomatic note about a civil suit filed by SFJ member Pannun regarding an alleged plot to assassinate him.Summons served by US court said to be ‘routine, procedural step’The summons naming Doval and Goel among the defendants seeks damages for an attempt on Pannun’s life and was delivered to the Indian embassy in Washington on Oct 9. Sources described the move as a “routine, procedural step”. They said this was not the first time such a summons had been served by US courts.Former PM Manmohan Singh was served with a civil summons in 2013 in connection with a suit filed by the same outfit, SFJ, alleging human rights violations related to 1984. In 2013, a federal court in Washington DC had issued summons to Singh during his visit to Washington. Former Chinese President Jiang Zemin was also served a similar summons in 2002. Both suits were eventually dismissed.The court order in the Pannun case came ahead of the Nov 20 sentencing of Nikhil Gupta, an Indian national arrested by the US in the matter.The state department note also clarified that the action was carried out in compliance with court instructions and does not indicate any US position on the case.“The performance of state department of its statutory functions under 28 USC (US Codes). 1608 should not be construed as an indication in any way of the US’s’ position or views on whether plaintiffs have properly complied with all statutory requirements of the FSIA (Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act), the status or character of a defendant, whether service was properly effected, or the merits of any claims or defenses,” it said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bihar parties eye UP turf, but poll gains won’t be easy
articles.summary: Bihar parties like LJP(RV) and JD(U) aim to contest UP’s 2027 polls, but past results show weak cross-state appeal and NDA ally turf tensions with SBSP.
articles.body: Lucknow: Despite attempts by parties based in UP and Bihar to emerge as players in each other’s political turf, past election results suggest these cross-border ambitions have produced little electoral success.The latest attempt is being made by the Chirag Paswan-led Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas), a BJP ally, which has signalled its willingness to contest all 403 assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh, if it is not accommodated in BJP-led NDA for the 2027 Assembly elections.Addressing the ‘Nav Sankalp Mahasabha’ in Varanasi earlier this week, Paswan asked party workers to expand the organisation’s footprint in UP and build a support base ahead of the 2027 state polls. His assertion is being seen as an attempt to increase the party’s bargaining power within NDA even as it seeks a foothold in a state where his party’s presence remains limitedChirag’s party, which was formed in 2021 after the split from the original Lok Jan Shakti Party, contested 21 seats in the 2022 UP elections but lost deposits on all seats while securing barely 0.01% of the votes.This was one of the lowest performances by a state party in the UP elections. At that time, LJP(RV) was not part of NDA — it joined the saffron bandwagon in 2023. Chirag, Lok Sabha MP from Bihar’s Hajipur, was later inducted into the Modi cabinet.JD(U) politician and Bihar minister Nishant Kumar, son of former CM Nitish Kumar, too, recently claimed that his party would contest UP elections as an ally of NDA. Rajbhar went on to claim that his party would be forced to consider “other options” if LJP (RV) finds a place in the BJP-led alliance. The warning was seen as a reflection of an emerging turf battle within NDA, where regional allies are increasingly conscious of protecting their political space and electoral constituencies.SBSP spokesperson Piyush Mishra said his party was not included in NDA alliance during the 2025 Bihar elections. “The treatment meted out to his party should be given to the Bihar’s outfits as well,” Mishra said.Nudged out of NDA, the SBSP contested 27 Assembly seats in Bihar but faced a complete rout, while bagging barely 0.12% of the votes.Political experts said the contrasting experiences of these parties underline a larger reality — regional influence does not necessarily travel across state boundaries, even when neighbouring states share social and cultural linkages.While caste identities and community networks often extend beyond geographical boundaries, especially in the case of UP and Bihar, their electoral mobilisation is shaped by state-specific political equations, local leadership, organisational structures and established loyalties.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: A Louisiana man acquired an early stake linked to Raising Cane's before marrying in 2001; after their 2007 divorce settlement, his former wife sought a share of the interests, but a 2026 appeals court rejected her claim
articles.summary: A business investment made before marriage can become the subject of a legal dispute years after a couple separates, particularly when the ownership
articles.body: A business investment made before marriage can become the subject of a legal dispute years after a couple separates, particularly when the ownership structure changes during the marriage. In Louisiana, an early investment connected to the popular restaurant chain Raising Cane's became the focus of a dispute between a divorced couple over whether the former wife could claim a share of her ex-husband's business interests. On November 6, 2026, the Louisiana Court of Appeal, Fourth Circuit, rejected her attempt to reopen the division of their property. The ruling in Anne Treme McQueen v. John Blackshear McQueen, available on Justia, upheld a lower court decision finding that the couple's 2007 consent judgment had already allocated property titled in each spouse's name, including the disputed business interests.How the Raising Cane's investment beganAccording to the court's opinion, John McQueen acquired 10,000 preferred shares in Lloyd Bartlett, Inc. before marrying Anne McQueen on October 20, 2001. The corporation was connected to Todd Graves' restaurant business, which developed into Raising Cane's. The business structure changed shortly after the marriage. In November 2001, New LB, Inc. was established as part of a restructuring involving the Raising Cane's-related entities. Lloyd Bartlett, Inc. merged into New LB, which survived the transaction and subsequently adopted the Lloyd Bartlett name.Under the restructuring arrangement, John's original 10,000 preferred shares were exchanged for shares in the surviving corporation and membership interests in three limited liability companies: Raising Cane's Restaurants, LLC, Raising Cane's USA, LLC and Raising Cane's Franchising, LLC. The court's opinion described the interests received in the exchange as a 2% stake in the corporation and a 1% interest in each of the three LLCs. A later affidavit submitted by John reported a 0.495% interest in each LLC.What the 2007 divorce settlement coveredAnne filed for divorce on November 9, 2006. The divorce was finalised through a judgment signed on September 4, 2007. The former couple subsequently entered into a consent judgment on October 24, 2007, addressing the division of their community property. The agreement recognised Anne's ownership of the former family home and provided that each spouse would retain sole ownership of property in their possession or titled in their respective names. It also covered property attributable to their work or employment.The settlement listed several examples, including vehicles, bank accounts, investment accounts, retirement assets, intellectual property and personal property. Both parties waived further claims concerning community property, including requests for accounting and reimbursement. However, the agreement did not specifically name Lloyd Bartlett, Inc. or the three Raising Cane's-related companies. Nor did it provide a separate valuation or detailed ownership breakdown of John's business interests.Why the former wife returned to courtOn May 28, 2025, Anne filed a motion seeking the partition of property she believed had not been divided during the divorce. Her claims included John's interests in Lloyd Bartlett, Inc. and the three Raising Cane's-related companies.She argued that the business interests had not been specifically addressed in the 2007 settlement. According to her position, the agreement did not identify the companies, establish the ownership percentages or disclose their value. She also maintained that although she knew John had a connection to Raising Cane's, she did not understand the nature or extent of his interests.John opposed the motion, arguing that the consent judgment had already settled the matter by awarding each spouse property titled in their respective names. He maintained that Anne could not reopen the property division to claim interests held in his name.How the appeals court interpreted the agreementThe dispute required the Fourth Circuit to examine Louisiana's res judicata law, including La. R.S. 13:4232(B), which addresses the application of res judicata in divorce and community-property proceedings. The court agreed that the provision was relevant but concluded that the wording of the consent judgment had already allocated the disputed interests. Because the corporate shares and LLC membership interests were titled in John's name, they fell within the agreement's provision awarding each spouse property held in their respective names.Anne also relied on a July 31, 2007 email exchange between John and his divorce lawyer. In the correspondence, John indicated that he wanted Anne to have as little involvement as possible in the matter. She argued that the communication was relevant to whether the business interests had been disclosed or addressed during the divorce proceedings.However, the appellate court noted that the email had not been admitted into evidence. It also found that the correspondence did not establish a mutual agreement to exclude the business interests from the settlement or demonstrate that considering it would have changed the outcome. Importantly, the court did not determine whether John's interests were separate or community property, or establish their financial value. Its decision focused on whether Anne could pursue another partition claim after the 2007 agreement.Court upholds dismissal of the claimThe Louisiana Court of Appeal, Fourth Circuit, found no basis to overturn the lower court's decision. It affirmed the March 4, 2026 judgment sustaining John's exception of res judicata and dismissing Anne's motion to partition the disputed interests with prejudice.The November 6, 2026 ruling means Anne cannot reopen the property division to pursue the Raising Cane's-related interests covered by the settlement. The decision leaves the original consent judgment in place without determining the underlying classification or value of John's business holdings.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Meghan Markle's father, Thomas, cut off ankle monitor after arrest for alleged possession of child sexual abuse material, DOJ says
articles.summary: The 82-year-old, who appeared in a Tampa court last week, was under house arrest in Florida.
articles.body:
Meghan Markle's estranged father, Thomas Markle , cut off his ankle monitor while on house arrest after being charged with having child sexual abuse material, federal authorities said on Tuesday.

"Four days ago, a federal judge allowed Mr. Markle to remain out of custody pending trial," Bill Essayli, first assistant U.S. attorney for the Central District of California, said in a statement posted to X . "He was ordered to wear a location monitoring device. He allegedly cut the bracelet off at 1:45 a.m. last night. Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions. We are asking the court to revoke his release and detain him pending trial, and we will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law."

A Justice Department spokesperson told the BBC that Markle, 82, appeared in court in Tampa, Fla., on Tuesday after he allegedly removed his ankle monitor. He was reportedly ordered jailed without bond and remains in federal custody.

Last Friday, Markle appeared in federal court in Tampa, hours after FBI agents arrested him at his care home. He was charged with one count of possession of child pornography. He arrived at court in a wheelchair and did not enter a plea.

A magistrate judge released him on his own recognizance to home detention with electronic monitoring and barred him from traveling outside Florida's Middle District and California's Central District. The judge also ordered him to have no contact with minors and not to use devices that can access the internet, and to undergo a psychiatric evaluation before the case moved forward.

According to the Justice Department, Markle was arrested after agents discovered approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives and books, that contained suspected child sexual abuse material (CSAM) while searching two storage units registered to Markle, at least one of which was in the Los Angeles area.

"Mr. Markle is accused of possessing child sexual abuse material, including photographs depicting himself with minor girls," Essayli said in a press release announcing his initial arrest. "These allegations are extremely serious, and we will prosecute Mr. Markle to the fullest extent of federal law."

In October 2026, federal law enforcement learned that an individual signed an affidavit regarding the discovery of suspected CSAM among Markle's possessions in the Philippines, according to the press release. Officers then interviewed a separate individual who revealed Markle had rented a storage unit in the Los Angeles area.

This led to the discovery of a second storage unit. Both had been rented by Markle since 2008.

In a statement, FBI Director Kash Patel said that Markle "allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions."

"This FBI will use every single resource at our disposal to protect innocent kids — any predator who targets children will have zero safe haven in this country or anywhere they try to hide," Patel added.

If convicted, Markle could face a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison.

"This case highlights the importance of the involvement of the public, even if it's a family member or close friend, to be vigilant and speak up if they have information on individuals they suspect may be preying on and exploiting our children," said Patrick Grandy, the assistant director in charge of the FBI's Los Angeles Field Office.

In October, it was reported that Markle was under investigation in the Philippines over allegations that he possessed child sexual abuse material. Philippine authorities plan to file their own charges against him as early as Monday, ITV News reported.

The Sun first reported that his son, Meghan's half-brother Thomas Markle Jr., told Philippine police that after his father left the country in May, he discovered images of child sexual abuse material among boxes at his father's former home in Cebu.

Markle Sr. denied those allegations, telling the Daily Mail on Oct. 23: "It's just a bunch of lies. It's sick."

Markle is believed to have returned to the U.S. in May, after his left leg was amputated in the Philippines in December 2025. In October, The Sun reported Markle moved into Maravida Senior Living care home, a facility which specializes in "memory care."

Meghan Markle released a statement following the claims, saying she was "deeply distressed." She also revealed that in 2019 she received a copy of a letter containing "troubling" allegations about him, which had been sent to London's Metropolitan Police.

"It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated," she said. British police subsequently said it had not shared the letter with other law enforcement agencies.

According to the Sun on Sunday , Meghan was advised that speaking publicly could jeopardize any potential legal case.

Addressing her decision to keep Archie and Lilibet away from their grandfather over the past few years, Meghan said that "any distance from my father, and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them."

She added: "My sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children."

Meghan reportedly wrote to her estranged father in December 2025 to tell him she was aware of child abuse allegations against him and would not allow him to meet his grandchildren. Meghan reportedly told her father the letter would be the last time he heard from her.

articles.title: 'I've Had It' host Jennifer Welch cheers Wisconsin brewing company that called Kirk an 'awful human being'
articles.summary: Jennifer Welch promoted the Minocqua Brewing Company on her "I've Had It" podcast after the Wisconsin anti-Trump brewery attacked Charlie Kirk and offered sponsorship.
articles.body: "I've Had It" podcast host Jennifer Welch endorsed the anti-Trump Wisconsin brewery Minocqua Brewing Company on her podcast Tuesday after it referred to Turning Point USA (TPUSA) founder Charlie Kirk as a "racist jerk" and "awful human being." The show's producer, Kiley Josey, read a Facebook post from Sunday from the business attacking sponsors for pulling their support of Welch after she and co-host Angie Sullivan laughed at a joke about digging up Kirk's body after his assassination last year. In the post, Minocqua Brewing Company offered to support the podcast with a sponsorship, attacking Kirk in the process. LIBERAL PODCASTERS TELL TPUSA TO ‘F--- OFF’ AS CHARLIE KIRK BACKLASH COSTS THEM ADVERTISERS "Charlie Kirk was an awful human being, and everybody who’s not in a cult or a paid influencer on the right realizes that," the post read. "We’re sorry you’ve lost a few sponsors because you laughed at a joke about this racist jerk. We probably don’t have as much money as the sponsors you lost, but we’d love to step in and partner with you if you'll have us." "That is so sweet," Welch said. "Well, Minocqua Brewing Company, shout out to you and no money necessary. We are happy to promote your products and everybody in Wisconsin if you're … I don't know if their products are online, but hit up the Minocqua Brewing Company." Josey also described how the brewery has sold merchandise attacking President Donald Trump and the Republican Party, earning more praise from Welch. WELCH DOUBLES DOWN ON TPUSA FEUD, CALLS GROUP 'LOSERS' AFTER LAUGHING AT JOKE ABOUT KILLING CHARLIE KIRK AGAIN "Anti-Trump merch. You know what? I mean free ads for them forever. Forever. They're doing the good work. And I love a business that says we stand on business, and we're not going to tolerate our customer base being treated like s---. If other businesses could only say the same," Welch said. Minocqua Brewing Company previously gained nationwide attention after promoting a deal for "free beer, all day long" on the day Trump dies. The company doubled down on the deal after a foiled attack at the White House Correspondents' Dinner in April. "Well, we almost got #freebeerday," the company's post at the time said. "Either a brother or sister in the Resistance needs to work on their marksmanship or he faked another assassination to get a positive news cycle. We’ll never know." FBI, SECRET SERVICE PROBE WISCONSIN BREWERY OWNER OVER FREE BEER OFFER AFTER ALLEGED TRUMP KILLING ATTEMPT In a comment to Fox News Digital, Welch clarified, "We have never heard of Minocqua Brewing Company before today. Neither of us drink. Several listeners tagged us in a post from this company, and we read the post on the show without knowing of their previous comments. We have no relationship with this company and don’t intend to have one." TPUSA spokesperson Andrew Kolvet told Fox News Digital, "Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan have nobody to blame but themselves for the fact that their sponsors are cutting ties. Rather than accept responsibility for their own behavior, they want to blame Turning Point for noticing. "The organization didn’t coordinate this boycott; it happened organically. Everyday Americans were fed up with the fact they consistently laugh at, snicker, sneer and generally glorify assassination culture on their podcast. The audience — and their sponsors — are shouting at them that there is a line and they crossed it. They just refuse to listen."
